A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Training-Free Bayesianization (TFB) work. All pages, including appendices and v3's checklist, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, figures, and tables can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM evaluations, calibration results, computational measurements, ablations, and a toy regression experiment in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds MonteCLoRA evaluations in Table 1 and a test-time sample-count study in Appendix F.2.

M1.justification: The SVD transformation, low-rank isotropic posterior, variance-maximization search, and prediction procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The existing LoRA-variant and last-layer adaptations are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six commonsense reasoning tasks, Combined dataset, OBQA-to-ARC/MMLU distribution shifts, and toy regression task. The new sampling study uses the existing WG-S benchmark without introducing different task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds MonteCLoRA as an evaluated comparator in Table 1 alongside the retained MCD, ENS, LAP, BLoB, and deterministic baselines. Comparator membership in the detailed appendix tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F.2 adds a Llama3.1-8B evaluation on WG-S varying test-time samples up to N=160, with BLoB-Mean identified as the N=0 reference. The main N=10 protocol, data splits, training budgets, and variance-search settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a test-time sample-count sensitivity study in Appendix F.2 and Figure 3. The former computational analysis is moved to Section 5.3, while the existing anchor-size, anchor-source, distribution-family, and last-layer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already specify means and standard deviations over three random seeds in Appendix E.4. The new sampling study and checklist follow that practice; they introduce no different uncertainty-estimation procedure or per-experiment seed count.

E6.justification: v3 adds MonteCLoRA's ACC/ECE/NLL results in Table 1, including WG-S accuracy of 69.20±0.18%, and Figure 3's sampling curves showing generally better calibration with more samples. Matched pre-existing table values, including the relocated efficiency measurements, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 4.1, Theorems 4.1–4.2, and the appendix derivations are retained. Lemma D.1 moves inside the proof of Theorem 4.1, and Equations 14–15 exchange numbering without changing their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free LoRA Bayesianization, equivalence to generalized variational inference under stated conditions, and improved uncertainty estimation.

C2.justification: New Appendix F.2 interprets the sampling results as supporting N=10 as a performance–efficiency compromise, with a mild remaining gap to much larger sample counts. The existing limitations and interpretations of distribution shifts and computational efficiency are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract changes 'Code will be available' to 'Code is available.' However, v3's new checklist item 5 says code is not provided and will be released after acceptance, leaving availability internally inconsistent. Existing implementation and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sengupta et al.'s work on Bayesian reparameterization of low-rank adaptation as reference 51 for MonteCLoRA. All 69 earlier references remain, and the substantive positioning in Section 2 and Appendix C is unchanged.

P1.justification: The efficiency discussion moves from Appendix F.2 to Section 5.3 with condensed wording, and Lemma D.1 is repositioned within its proof. Local copyedits, acknowledgments, and a NeurIPS checklist are added; most scientific prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from the appendix to Section 3, and the efficiency table moves into the main text. v3 adds the sampling plot as Figure 3, renumbers the anchor-size plot, and adds MonteCLoRA rows and blue improvement highlighting to Table 1.

improvement.justification: The added MonteCLoRA comparison and sampling study modestly strengthen the empirical evaluation and support the existing N=10 choice. These targeted gains outweigh the limited documentation harm from contradictory code-release statements. The method, theory, and earlier results remain stable, and improved code access cannot be established from the PDFs.
